paragraphs: Why can a simple model sometimes match a complicated one on a noisy dataset? This paper studies that question through the Rashomon set: the collection of models with approximately equal predictive performance. The Rashomon ratio measures how much of the available model space belongs to this collection. A large ratio means many different models are competitive.

The authors investigate a mechanism connecting data generation with choices practitioners make during training. They demonstrate that noisier datasets can produce larger Rashomon ratios through this interaction. The explanation therefore concerns both the data and the way models are trained, rather than treating the number of competitive models as a property of noise alone.

The paper also introduces pattern diversity, which measures average prediction differences between distinct classification patterns within the Rashomon set. It explains why this diversity tends to grow with label noise. Together, these results help explain why simpler models often remain competitive on complex, noisy datasets, while also showing that similar overall accuracy can coexist with different predictions.
neurips-2023-a-path-to-simpler-models-st.tldr: The paper connects noise and training choices to the abundance of similarly accurate models, helping explain why simpler models often remain competitive.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning builds controllers from previously collected data. This can reduce the need to learn through potentially risky interactions with a real system. In settings such as healthcare, however, a controller also needs to make its decisions accountable. This paper addresses how a learned decision can be connected to examples in the data used to support it.

The proposed Accountable Offline Controller treats the offline dataset as a Decision Corpus. For control, it makes a tailored selection of examples called the Corpus Subset. These examples form the basis of its accountable decision process, giving the corpus a direct role in control rather than using it only as material for training.

The authors report that the approach works effectively when data are limited, combines conservative behavior with adaptability, and extends to strictly offline imitation. Evaluations cover simulated and real-world healthcare scenarios. The reported findings support the possibility of maintaining strong offline control performance while grounding decisions in selected examples, which is the paper's central approach to accountability.
neurips-2023-accountability-in-offline-r.tldr: AOC grounds offline control decisions in selected examples from its dataset to combine performance with accountability.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks can be disrupted by adversarial changes to node information or to the connections between nodes. This paper investigates whether the dynamics underlying a graph network help explain its resistance to these changes. It examines networks derived from different neural flows and relates them to several mathematical notions of stability.

A central argument is that Lyapunov stability, despite its common use, does not necessarily imply adversarial robustness. The authors therefore examine other stability properties as well, including bounded-input bounded-output, structural, and conservative stability. Drawing on physics, they propose constructing graph networks using conservative Hamiltonian neural flows.

Experiments compare different neural-flow graph networks across several benchmark datasets and multiple adversarial attacks. The authors report substantially improved robustness for networks combining conservative Hamiltonian flows with Lyapunov stability. This supports the proposed combination empirically, while the conceptual contribution is to separate different meanings of stability: a model satisfying one stability notion need not automatically resist adversarial changes to graph inputs.
neurips-2023-adversarial-robustness-in-g.tldr: Conservative Hamiltonian graph networks improve robustness in experiments, while the paper argues that Lyapunov stability alone does not ensure adversarial robustness.

paragraphs: This paper studies optimization when controlling an experiment's inputs has a cost. At each step, the learner chooses which variables to control and assigns their values. The remaining variables are sampled randomly. Different subsets carry different costs, so the learner must decide both what settings to try and how much control to purchase.

This creates a tradeoff between directing an evaluation and conserving the available budget. Choosing an informative subset can make learning more targeted, while leaving variables random can make an evaluation cheaper. The authors introduce this problem as Bayesian optimization with cost-varying variable subsets and develop an algorithm based on Gaussian processes and upper confidence bounds.

The algorithm has a theoretical no-regret guarantee, and the analysis examines how cheaper control subsets can support exploration and reduce accumulated regret. Empirically, the method finds significantly better solutions than comparable baselines under equal budgets. The contribution is to make the cost of controlling variables part of the optimization decision itself, alongside the choice of their values.
neurips-2023-bayesian-optimization-with-.tldr: The proposed Bayesian optimization method balances informative input control against its cost and offers a no-regret guarantee.

paragraphs: Generating an image from a new viewpoint is difficult when only a few views of the subject are available. Pretrained image diffusion models provide strong knowledge about visual appearance, but their lack of three-dimensional awareness can produce distorted geometry or alter the subject's identity. DreamSparse combines this image knowledge with spatial information extracted from the available views.

Its geometry module captures spatial features from the sparse input images, supplying a three-dimensional prior. A separate spatial guidance model converts rendered feature maps into information that guides image generation. The pretrained diffusion model remains frozen, allowing the framework to use its existing visual knowledge while encouraging consistency with the recovered spatial structure.

The framework handles both individual objects and object-centric scenes, and the authors report generalization to open-set images. Experiments show better novel-view synthesis than the tested baselines for both trained and open-set categories. The approach matters because it provides geometric guidance to a strong image generator without requiring further tuning of that pretrained diffusion model.
neurips-2023-dreamsparse-escaping-from-p.tldr: DreamSparse guides a frozen diffusion model with spatial features from sparse views to generate more geometrically and identity-consistent viewpoints.

paragraphs: Recurrent spiking neural networks draw inspiration from nervous systems and can represent complex dynamics. Training them commonly relies on surrogate gradients, which the authors identify as inaccurate and poorly suited to neuromorphic hardware. This paper proposes evolving connectivity as an alternative that trains through inference evaluations without requiring gradient calculations.

The framework changes what the optimization procedure searches over. Instead of directly adjusting individual weights, it searches parameterized probability distributions over connections. Natural Evolution Strategies optimize these distributions. The resulting design uses sparse Boolean connections and is intended to scale well, making the network's connectivity central to both learning and hardware compatibility.

On standard robotic locomotion tasks, the method performs comparably to deep neural networks and better than the tested gradient-trained spiking networks, including solving a 17-degree-of-freedom humanoid task. It also achieves a two- to threefold efficiency improvement over directly evolving parameters. These findings support connectivity search as a practical training alternative and a foundation for further energy-efficient spiking-network applications.
neurips-2023-evolving-connectivity-for-r.tldr: Evolving connectivity trains spiking networks by optimizing connection distributions, achieving strong locomotion results without gradients.

paragraphs: Retrospective decision analysis asks what might have happened if different actions had been taken earlier. For a treatment sequence, this could mean identifying decisions that would have improved a patient's modeled outcome. Previous methods focused on finitely many discrete states; this paper addresses settings where states vary continuously while actions remain discrete.

The authors describe these sequences using finite-horizon Markov decision processes and a broad class of bijective structural causal models. Within that framework, they define the problem of finding a counterfactually optimal action sequence. They also establish a computational obstacle: in general, a polynomial-time solution cannot be expected.

The proposed search method builds on A*. Under a Lipschitz continuity condition on the environment's dynamics, it is guaranteed to return the optimal solution to the formulated problem. Experiments using real clinical data find the method efficient in practice. The contribution therefore combines an explicit causal formulation, a conditional optimality guarantee, and evidence that exact search can be practical despite the problem's general computational difficulty.
neurips-2023-finding-counterfactually-op.tldr: An A*-based method finds counterfactually optimal discrete action sequences in continuous-state models under a Lipschitz continuity condition.

paragraphs: Synthetic glucose traces need to reproduce useful characteristics of real measurements while protecting the people whose data informed them. The authors argue that existing time-series generators struggle with the distinctive structure of glucose data and lose substantial utility when formal privacy protection is added. GlucoSynth addresses these two requirements within a single generative framework.

The method uses a generative adversarial network designed to preserve more than temporal dynamics alone. It also aims to conserve relationships among motifs, meaning glucose events within a trace. This makes the connections between events an explicit part of the generation approach. Differential privacy mechanisms supply formal privacy guarantees.

The evaluation uses 1.2 million glucose traces to examine the real-world utility of the synthetic data. The authors report that GlucoSynth surpasses previous methods in generating high-quality glucose traces with strong privacy guarantees. The findings support modeling event relationships as part of private time-series synthesis, with glucose data serving as the demonstrated application and other time-series sources identified as potential extensions.
neurips-2023-glucosynth-generating-diffe.tldr: GlucoSynth preserves glucose-event relationships and temporal dynamics to generate useful synthetic traces with differential privacy guarantees.

paragraphs: Motion planning seeks a high-quality path through a robot's possible configurations while avoiding collisions. Graph neural networks can learn useful information from the graph used for planning, but extracting graph patterns and searching for a route are different requirements. The authors identify a mismatch between the mechanism of an existing leading GNN planner and the graph-search process.

GraphMP addresses that mismatch through a customized network architecture and training mechanism. It is designed to combine efficient graph-pattern extraction with graph-search processing in one neural planner. The intended scope includes both low-dimensional problems and higher-dimensional tasks involving more complex robotic configurations.

Experiments range from a two-dimensional maze to a 14-dimensional dual KUKA robotic arm. Across the evaluated environments, the authors report significant improvements in path quality and planning speed over leading learning-based and classical planners, while maintaining a competitive success rate. The findings suggest that adapting the network to the search process can improve planning efficiency without giving up competitive reliability in finding a path.
neurips-2023-graphmp-graph-neural-networ.tldr: GraphMP combines graph feature learning with search-oriented processing to improve robotic path quality and planning speed.

paragraphs: Information Pursuit selects queries greedily according to how much information they provide about an output, but estimating that information in high dimensions is expensive. Orthogonal Matching Pursuit instead builds a sparse signal representation by repeatedly choosing the dictionary element most correlated with what remains unexplained. This paper establishes a connection between these two selection procedures.

For Information Pursuit using random projections of dictionary atoms as queries, the authors show that the procedure nearly reduces to Orthogonal Matching Pursuit. The remaining difference is a normalization of correlation gain. They call the resulting method IP-OMP. Simulations with random Gaussian dictionaries suggest that this difference has no appreciable effect on sparse-code recovery.

The authors then use IP-OMP for explainable image prediction. An image is represented through a small combination of text embeddings corresponding to interpretable concepts. Prediction uses the combination's weights, which also provide the explanation. Experiments find the method competitive with existing explainability approaches and less computationally expensive, connecting an information-based interpretation to a practical sparse representation.
neurips-2023-information-maximization-pe.tldr: The paper connects information-based query selection to sparse coding and uses that connection for efficient, concept-based image explanations.

paragraphs: Semi-supervised learning uses unlabeled examples alongside labeled data. A common approach assigns predicted labels to unlabeled examples and trains on those predictions when confidence is high enough. Because an incorrect predicted label can enter the training set, the rule deciding which examples to accept is central to the method.

InstanT makes that acceptance threshold depend on each individual example. Existing adaptive approaches commonly share a threshold across all examples or across members of a class. The proposed function instead uses an example's ambiguity and its instance-dependent pseudo-label error rate. Examples more likely to receive an incorrect label must clear a higher confidence threshold.

The authors also establish a bounded probabilistic guarantee for the correctness of labels assigned through their threshold function. This provides a mathematical basis for connecting acceptance decisions to individual uncertainty. The contribution is a finer-grained way to select training examples: confidence requirements can vary within a class, reflecting differences between examples that a shared threshold would overlook.
neurips-2023-instant-semi-supervised-lea.tldr: InstanT sets individual pseudo-label confidence thresholds using example ambiguity and error rates, with a bounded probabilistic correctness guarantee.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning can improve a language model's reward while degrading other aspects of its behavior. This paper argues that evaluating alignment requires measuring the tradeoff between reward and drift, because reward improvement alone can conceal undesirable changes. It proposes Elastic Reset to improve that tradeoff without explicitly changing the training objective.

The algorithm maintains an exponential moving average of the online model. Periodically, it resets the online model to that average and then resets the average model to the initial model. The authors report that averaging helps the online model recover quickly after each reset, achieving more reward with less drift over the same number of training steps.

Results cover a small pivot-translation benchmark, a medium-scale simulated sentiment-alignment task, and a technical question-answering chatbot built with LLaMA-7B. Elastic Reset achieves the reported leading or improved performance in these settings. The work makes the training trajectory itself a means of managing reward and drift, with empirical evidence across several scales and task types.
neurips-2023-language-model-alignment-wi.tldr: Elastic Reset periodically resets model weights through a moving average to achieve higher alignment reward with less drift in the evaluated tasks.

paragraphs: MosaicBERT addresses the cost of pretraining a custom BERT-style language encoder. The authors combine architectural and training advances into a design optimized empirically for fast pretraining. The aim is to make training a specialized encoder from scratch more accessible to researchers and engineers.

The architecture incorporates FlashAttention, linear attention biases, gated linear units, dynamic removal of padded tokens, and low-precision LayerNorm. Its training recipe uses a 30% masked-token ratio, bfloat16 precision, and a vocabulary size chosen for GPU throughput, alongside practices from other encoder models. Efficiency is therefore pursued through both model operations and training configuration.

When pretrained on C4, the base model reaches an average GLUE development score of 79.6 after 1.13 hours on eight A100 80 GB GPUs, at a reported cost of roughly $20. Accuracy-versus-speed comparisons place both base and large MosaicBERT models on the Pareto frontier against competitive BERT counterparts. These results demonstrate favorable measured tradeoffs between pretraining time and downstream accuracy for the tested configurations.
neurips-2023-mosaicbert-a-bidirectional-.tldr: MosaicBERT combines efficient encoder components and a tuned training recipe to improve the measured tradeoff between pretraining speed and accuracy.

paragraphs: Designing a nonlinear controller requires more than observing good behavior in simulations when stability must be guaranteed. One approach pairs a control policy with a Lyapunov function that certifies stability. This paper develops a method for learning neural Lyapunov control across a broad class of discrete-time systems, extending beyond earlier continuous-time or narrowly restricted settings.

Three components support the method. A mixed-integer linear programming procedure verifies the discrete-time stability conditions. Another procedure computes verified sublevel sets, identifying certified portions of the state space. A gradient-based heuristic quickly searches for counterexamples, helping the learning process discover where a candidate certificate fails and speeding up its improvement.

Across four standard benchmarks, the authors report significant gains over leading baselines. On path tracking, both runtime and region-of-attraction size improve by an order of magnitude over recent neural Lyapunov methods. For cartpole and PVTOL, they report the first automated approach to return a provably stable controller. The results connect faster certificate learning with larger verified regions of stable behavior.
neurips-2023-neural-lyapunov-control-for.tldr: The method combines neural learning and formal verification to produce provably stable controllers for a broad class of discrete-time systems.

paragraphs: In conventional federated learning, clients train model parameters locally and periodically send parameters for server aggregation. The same representation therefore serves two purposes: learning from local data and communicating across clients. This paper argues that these purposes can impose conflicting requirements on which parameters should be used.

FedSep separates them into a learning layer and a communication layer for each client. Encoding and decoding operations connect the layers, with decoding formulated as a minimization problem. The authors express the overall framework as a federated bilevel optimization problem and develop an efficient algorithm to solve it.

The theoretical analysis shows convergence matching standard federated learning algorithms. Experiments report stronger performance than various baselines on communication-efficient learning and learning with heterogeneous models. These applications illustrate why the separation matters: clients can use distinct arrangements for local learning and shared communication, while the connecting optimization maintains a relationship between them. The contribution is a framework for resolving the competing requirements through explicit separation.
neurips-2023-resolving-the-tug-of-war-a-.tldr: FedSep separates local learning parameters from communication representations while matching standard federated convergence and improving tested applications.

paragraphs: A smaller pretrained model can provide an initialization for a larger model, reducing the resources needed to train the larger one. This paper examines how to transfer that information more completely. The authors argue that methods mapping only portions of the weights can miss interactions within and between the pretrained and target models.

Their proposed method linearly relates each target weight to all weights in the pretrained model. That broader mapping is intended to capture relationships overlooked by partial mappings. To make it affordable, the method uses multi-linear operators that reduce computational and storage complexity, keeping the transfer's resource requirements manageable.

In experiments transferring from DeiT-small to DeiT-base, the authors report a 76% reduction in computational cost. They report that this saving exceeds those of bert2BERT and LiGO in the comparison. The result supports the value of considering model-wide weight relationships during growth, while the structured operators address the practical cost of using such a comprehensive mapping.
neurips-2023-reusing-pretrained-models-b.tldr: Structured multi-linear mappings reuse model-wide weight relationships to initialize larger models and reduce training costs.

paragraphs: This paper studies the statistical accuracy of score matching and how that accuracy affects causal discovery. Its focus is sample complexity: relating the amount of available data to the quality of an estimated score function. The contribution supplies theoretical bounds for an estimation procedure that also plays a role in generative modeling.

The authors demonstrate that a standard deep ReLU neural network trained with stochastic gradient descent can accurately estimate the score function. They then analyze a score-matching-based causal discovery method and bound its errors in recovering causal relationships. This second result assumes a sufficiently accurate score estimate, making the dependency between estimation quality and causal recovery explicit.

The paper also develops an upper bound for score-matching estimation in score-based generative modeling. That analysis is relevant to its use in causal discovery and has independent significance for generative models. Together, the results connect neural score estimation to downstream statistical guarantees, with causal-recovery conclusions expressly conditioned on the quality of the score estimate.
neurips-2023-sample-complexity-bounds-fo.tldr: The paper bounds neural score-estimation accuracy and its implications for causal discovery and score-based generative modeling.

paragraphs: Approximate nearest-neighbor search uses an index to find nearby data points efficiently, accepting the possibility of missing the exact nearest point. Some indexing approaches reduce that risk by placing redundant representations into the data partitioning scheme. SOAR builds on this idea by changing how those representations are constructed.

Instead of training redundant representations independently, SOAR coordinates them using an orthogonality-amplified residual loss. Each representation is optimized to compensate for situations where the others perform poorly. Redundancy therefore becomes deliberately complementary: the additional representation is designed around weaknesses in the alternatives, rather than simply providing another independently computed version.

The authors report a large improvement in index quality and state-of-the-art results on approximate nearest-neighbor benchmarks, while retaining fast index construction and low memory use. These findings suggest that the organization of redundancy matters as much as its presence. The central contribution is an objective that makes multiple representations cover one another's failures, improving the overall search index under the evaluated conditions.
neurips-2023-soar-improved-indexing-for-.tldr: SOAR improves approximate nearest-neighbor indexing by training redundant representations to compensate for one another's weaknesses.

paragraphs: Synthetic data can supplement real training data when access is constrained by sensitivity, bias, or acquisition cost. Choosing a generator is complicated because synthetic-data research spans different data types and goals, including privacy, fairness, and augmentation. Synthcity addresses the practical difficulty of comparing methods across this fragmented landscape.

The contribution is an open-source Python library for benchmarking synthetic-data generators across modalities and use cases. It also provides a centralized collection of generators, bringing evaluation and access into the same toolkit. A plug-in API allows additional generators to be incorporated, so the framework can accommodate methods beyond its existing collection.

The paper demonstrates the framework through examples involving tabular generation and data augmentation. These examples illustrate its applicability and the insights obtainable from comparative evaluation. The main value is shared infrastructure for selecting and studying generators in context: users can compare methods according to the task they need synthetic data to serve, rather than treating generation quality as a single, universal requirement.
neurips-2023-synthcity-a-benchmark-frame.tldr: Synthcity provides an extensible library for accessing and benchmarking synthetic-data generators across data types and use cases.

paragraphs: Inverse molecular design starts with desired properties and searches for molecules that could provide them. Many algorithms address this challenge, but evaluating them meaningfully requires tasks that reflect practical chemistry. This paper identifies a gap between the growth of design algorithms and the development of realistic benchmarks for comparing them.

Tartarus supplies benchmark tasks based on physical simulations of molecular systems. The tasks mimic design problems involving materials, drugs, and chemical reactions. This connects evaluation to simulated physical behavior relevant to intended applications, giving researchers a common setting for testing how their algorithms explore chemical space.

The authors demonstrate the benchmark suite by comparing several established families of algorithms, illustrating both its utility and ease of use. The contribution is an evaluation platform rather than a claim that molecular design has been solved. Its intended impact is to bring algorithm development closer to practical design needs in research and industry by making realistic problem settings available for systematic comparison.
neurips-2023-tartarus-a-benchmarking-pla.tldr: Tartarus benchmarks molecular-design algorithms on physically simulated tasks intended to reflect practical chemistry problems.

paragraphs: A general deductive reasoner must handle proofs more complex than the examples it has seen. This paper tests that requirement in language models, extending beyond evaluations restricted to one deduction rule, a fixed proof size, or examples drawn from the same distribution as the demonstrations.

The authors create a synthetic, programmable dataset with control over deduction rules and proof complexity. They test generalization from simpler demonstrations along depth, width, and composition. This design allows them to examine different ways a proof can become more demanding, rather than collapsing reasoning ability into performance on one fixed collection of problems.

Experiments with four language models of different sizes and training objectives show that they can generalize to compositional proofs. They struggle with longer proofs, however, and need explicit demonstrations to produce hypothetical subproofs for proof by cases and contradiction. The results distinguish success at combining reasoning patterns from success at extending reasoning length or introducing the hypothetical structure required by certain proof methods.
neurips-2023-testing-the-general-deducti.tldr: Controlled proof tests show compositional generalization in four language models alongside difficulties with longer proofs and undemonstrated hypothetical subproofs.

paragraphs: Tensor neural networks with t-product layers have shown promise for multi-channel learning, but their generalization had lacked a corresponding theoretical analysis. This paper derives upper bounds on generalization error in both ordinary and adversarial settings, examining how weight structure affects the resulting guarantees.

A central result concerns exact low-rank parameterization in the transformed domain. Compressing a tensor network with this structure can yield tighter adversarial generalization bounds than an uncompressed model. Because exact transformed low-rank weights are uncommon in practice, the paper also develops sharp bounds for networks whose weights only approximately have that structure.

The authors further show that adversarial training through gradient flow can implicitly encourage transformed low-rank parameterization in highly over-parameterized ReLU tensor networks under certain conditions. This connects a potentially useful weight structure to a training mechanism that may favor it. The findings establish theoretical potential for better robust generalization, with the training result conditional and the compression benefit expressed through tighter error bounds.
neurips-2023-transformed-low-rank-parame.tldr: Transformed low-rank weights can tighten adversarial generalization bounds for tensor networks, and certain adversarial training dynamics can encourage that structure.

paragraphs: Type-to-Track lets users specify objects to follow in a video through natural-language descriptions. This changes the input to multiple-object tracking from boxes or category annotations to descriptions of the objects of interest. The approach aims to overcome some restrictions of those traditional ways of specifying targets.

The paper introduces GroOT, a dataset containing videos with varied objects and detailed captions describing appearance and action. It also defines two evaluation protocols and task-specific metrics. Together, these contributions establish a setting for studying grounded multiple-object tracking, where performance depends on following the objects referred to by text.

The proposed method, MENDER, uses a transformer-based embed-encode-extract framework with third-order tensor decomposition. Across five experimental scenarios, it outperforms a two-stage design in accuracy and efficiency, with reported improvements up to 14.7% in accuracy and fourfold speed. The work combines an interaction paradigm, evaluation resources, and a practical method, making language-directed tracking a concrete task that can be measured and compared.
neurips-2023-type-to-track-retrieve-any-.tldr: Type-to-Track introduces language-directed object tracking, a supporting dataset and evaluation setup, and an efficient transformer-based method.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning large language models requires memory for more than their trainable weights. The authors identify stored activations, which are needed for gradient calculations, as the primary training-memory bottleneck. Their approach reduces how much activation information must be retained by accepting carefully controlled noise in the gradient calculation.

The paper introduces unbiased estimators for matrix multiplication that require only sampled activations. Its motivation is that stochastic optimization can tolerate noisy gradients when estimates remain unbiased and their variance is reasonable. Both theoretical analysis and transformer-tuning experiments indicate lower estimator variance than existing alternatives.

Replacing transformer linear operations with the proposed approximation yields up to a 2.7-fold reduction in peak memory use with almost no accuracy loss, and permits batches up to 6.4 times larger. Under the same hardware constraints, the authors report improved downstream performance through larger models or faster training through larger batches. The contribution targets activation storage directly while using estimator design to control the optimization noise introduced by sampling.
neurips-2023-winner-take-all-column-row-.tldr: Unbiased, lower-variance sampling estimators reduce activation storage during transformer tuning, enabling substantial memory savings with little reported accuracy loss.

paragraphs: This paper addresses federated optimization problems that can be nonsmooth, nonconvex, or hierarchical. The hierarchical cases include bilevel and minimax problems, where the objective can depend implicitly on another optimization problem. That dependence makes analysis difficult when the implicit objective has no closed-form expression or lacks the smoothness assumed by earlier methods.

For nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization, the authors combine randomized smoothing with Clarke subdifferential calculus to develop a zeroth-order federated method. They derive communication and iteration bounds for reaching an approximate Clarke stationary point. This is a stationarity guarantee suited to nonsmooth problems, rather than a guarantee of finding a global optimum.

For the hierarchical cases, they develop a unified implicit zeroth-order framework with explicit complexity guarantees. The method delays some local calls to an inexact lower-level federated solver, reducing communication overhead. Experiments on nonsmooth and hierarchical machine-learning problems support the theory. The contribution combines broader optimization coverage with a specific mechanism for reducing the communication demanded by nested optimization.
neurips-2023-zeroth-order-methods-for-no.tldr: Randomized zeroth-order methods provide complexity guarantees for nonsmooth and hierarchical federated optimization while reducing lower-level communication.
